mods.description: The ColorLight mod replaces vanilla block lighting with lighting that matches each block's texture.

releases.notes:
# ColorLight — GPU Lighting Mode

ColorLight's colored light is applied on the graphics card: a Sodium shader looks up the light for every pixel instead of baking colour into chunk vertices. The light is smoother, and chunks are not rebuilt when it changes.

Light propagation is still computed on the CPU (the Lua methods `grid` and `smooth`). Only the application of light to pixels has been moved to the GPU.

---

## How it works

**Light volume on the GPU.** The light lives in a sparse volume around the camera, stored in two texel buffers (`GpuLightVolume`):

- **data**: a header (camera, flags, tint settings) and a list of sections, each holding a slot number or `-1`;
- **pool**: slots of 4096 cells (16 KiB each); only a section that holds light gets a slot. A cell stores the light colour `0x00BBGGRR` and a "solid block" bit.

Sections are addressed in a ring, so the window follows the camera without moving any data. The shader window is 31 sections horizontally and 15 vertically. A light change rewrites only a few KiB of video memory.

**Shader.** A copy of Sodium's terrain shader (`colored_terrain.vsh/.fsh`) with a shared include, `colorlight_data.glsl`. For every pixel it:

1. determines the face normal from screen-space derivatives;
2. reads the light colour and level from the volume (with smooth interpolation);
3. builds the final colour: vanilla lighting in which the part added by block light is recoloured to the source's colour.

Sky light is left untouched, so the tint washes out by day and is fully visible at night. Fully emissive faces (glowing models) stay vanilla.

**Sodium integration.** Three small mixins (`mixin/sodium`):

| Mixin | What it does |
|---|---|
| `ShaderChunkRendererMixin` | Adds the volume buffers and swaps the terrain shaders for ours |
| `SodiumWorldRendererMixin` | Passes the camera position to the volume once per frame |
| `DefaultChunkRendererMixin` | Binds the buffers for every terrain draw |

**Fallback.** The GPU mode turns on only if all three mixins applied (they are skipped for unverified Sodium versions). If anything goes wrong, the mod switches back to the vertex-colour mode on its own and re-meshes. The GPU mode is not used with Iris shader packs.

---

## Settings

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| Shader lighting (GPU) | Turns the mode on; applies immediately; unavailable while a shader pack is enabled |
| GPU light memory | How many 16×16×16 sections of light are kept on the graphics card (default 768, from 64 to 4096) |
| Tint vividness | How early the colour shows up and how far from the source it lasts |

**Tint vividness** (`tint_gamma`, 0–200%):

| Value | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| 0–20% | The colour is vivid and saturated all the way to the edge of the light; only the brightness falls off |
| 55% (default) | The colour lasts noticeably farther and weakens toward the edge |
| 100% and above | The colour fades together with the light; above 100% it stays subtle until a block is almost fully lit |

If the colour lasts too far or not far enough by default, change the line `float retention = clamp(1.0 - tintGamma, 0.0, 1.0);` in `colored_terrain.fsh`. The steepness of the whole slider is set by the `* 3.0` factor in the `exponent` line.

# ColorLight — GPU-режим освещения

Цветной свет ColorLight применяется на видеокарте: шейдер Sodium ищет свет для каждого пикселя, а не запекает цвет в вершины чанка. Свет получается плавнее, а при его изменении чанки не пересобираются.

Распространение света по-прежнему считается на CPU (Lua-методы `grid` и `smooth`). На GPU вынесено только применение света к пикселям.

---

## Как это работает

**Объём света на GPU.** Свет лежит в разреженном объёме вокруг камеры, в двух texel-буферах (`GpuLightVolume`):

# ColorLight — Optimization

What was changed, why it was changed, and how it was verified. The mod's public behavior (colors, range, modes, config, commands) has been preserved; differences are listed in the “Behavior Changes” section.

## 1. Dynamic Entity Lighting (Main Cause of Stutters)

**Before.** Every 1/8 block, an entity performed on the main thread: `removeSource` for up to 4 old points (each one traversing 26 neighbors in the *static* light field) + up to 4 separate SMOOTH fills + marking a cube of ~33³ blocks as “dirty.” Dynamic lighting lived in the same field as torches, so when their areas overlapped, “darkening” would overwrite parts of the static light.

**Now.**

* Dynamic lighting has been moved to a **separate layer** (`DynamicLightLayer`, `DynamicFootprint`). The final cell color = `max(static, dynamic)`. Light movement does **not touch the static field at all** — this eliminates lag when light circles overlap (verified: 0 static cells modified).
* All 4 corner points are filled in **a single pass**, rather than four.
* Filling runs in a **background thread** (`ColorLight Dynamic Light`); the main thread only constructs the “desired state.” Requests are merged per entity (the latest one wins), so the queue does not grow.
* Block changes inside an illuminated area mark the footprint as stale — the light is recalculated even if the entity is standing still.
* `findGlowingBlockSettings` no longer walks through the config `LinkedList` or parses an `Identifier` for every entity every tick — `ColorLightBlockRegistry` (`HashMap`) is used instead.

## 2. Static Lighting Engine

* All work is performed on primitives: packed `long` keys (`PosKey`, the same format as `BlockPos.asLong`), custom queues/hash maps. No `BlockPos.of/offset` and no `Long` boxing in hot loops.
* Block transparency and sub-unit SMOOTH precision are cached for the duration of a pass (`PassMap`): `getBlockState` is called once per cell instead of up to 26 times. Falloff tables are precomputed using the same float expressions (result is identical).
* Storage (`LightStorage`) uses 16×16×16 chunk columns without boxing or allocations during reads; it can unload an entire column and keeps a section “emptiness” counter.
* **Thread safety.** Previously, `APPLY_EXECUTOR` and the main thread could mutate the engine simultaneously without synchronization. Now all mutations are protected by a `ReentrantLock`, while reads (meshing) are lock-free. `drainDirtySections`, `getSourceSnapshot`, and `markRegionDirty` **never block** the calling thread.
* Batched chunk source insertion (`SourceBatch` → `addSources`) performs a single pass for a group of 8.
* Darkening (`darkenAndCollectSeeds`) only refills cells with *independent* light in the channel carried by the removed source (previously, any non-empty neighbor), and processes each cell only once.
* The “source” flag is stored in the cell's highest byte, so `hasSource` requires a single read with no hash map.

## 3. Rendering and Chunk Scanning

* **Precise section marking.** The engine itself knows which cells changed and marks only the sections whose meshes read them (cell ± 1 block). Previously, a chunk containing a source marked the entire vertical column (~380 sections) plus the light radius.
* `ColorLightDirtyFlusher`: once per tick, passes unique sections to the renderer, no more than 128 per tick, **closest to the player first** — spikes (entering the world, sunrise/sunset) are spread across multiple ticks.

releases.notes:
### This is a test of various lighting calculation methods. 

This test introduces a "circular" lighting calculation. This method is natively integrated into LDL, and the lighting can be applied to all blocks.

The GPU computing mode has been removed.

**WARNING**: When circular lighting is enabled alongside LDL, significant lag may occur if the light fields overlap; however, there will be no lag if circular lighting is turned off.
